Class KernelSHAP<T>

java.lang.Object
smile.feature.importance.KernelSHAP<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the data type of model input objects.
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, SHAP<T>
public class KernelSHAP<T> extends Object implements SHAP<T>, Serializable
Kernel SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is a model-agnostic method to approximate Shapley values using a specially-weighted local linear regression over feature coalitions.

Given an input instance x with M features and a background reference dataset B, Kernel SHAP evaluates the expected model prediction for sampled feature coalitions (where missing features are marginalized over the background dataset B) and solves a constrained weighted least squares problem that enforces the Shapley efficiency axiom: 

    sum_{j=1}^M phi_j = f(x) - E[f(z)]

References

  1. Lundberg, Scott M., and Su-In Lee. A unified approach to interpreting model predictions. NIPS, 2017.

    • shap

      public double[] shap(T rawInput)
      Description copied from interface: SHAP
      Returns the SHAP values. For regression, the length of SHAP values is same as the number of features. For classification, SHAP values are of p x k, where p is the number of features and k is the classes. The first k elements are the SHAP values of first feature over k classes, respectively. The rest features follow accordingly.
      Specified by:
      shap in interface SHAP<T>
      Parameters:
      rawInput - an instance.
      Returns:
      the SHAP values.
